    ResultBus ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Result data for a bus after running a fault calculation.

    Three physically distinct currents meet at a grounding bus, and mixing them up is the classic sizing error EN 50522 / IEC 61936-1 guard against:

    • i_inj — the current injected into the grounding system at this bus by the sources (at a source bus) or drawn out of it by the fault (at the fault bus). It flows through a lumped connection, the earthing conductor (Erdungsleiter), which therefore has to be sized for the full earth-fault current. Zero at every other bus.
    • ia — the share of that current which is actually dissipated into the soil at this bus, u_EPR / Z_B. It flows through the earth electrode (Erder) and is generally much smaller.
    • the branch shield currents, reported per branch on :class:ResultBranch.

    i_inj deliberately excludes the mutual Norton-equivalent injections of the inductively coupled branches: those model a distributed induced EMF along the line, not a current entering the node through a lumped conductor. The full nodal balance including them is ia = i_vector + sum_branches (u_other - u_self) * Y_self.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    name str

    The name of the bus.
    uepr float

    RMS earth potential rise at the bus, in volts.
    ia float

    RMS bus current dissipated into the soil through the earth electrode, in amperes.
    i_inj float

    RMS source-side injection at the bus, in amperes — the current carried by the earthing conductor. Defaults to 0.0 so that results stored before this field existed still validate.
    uepr_freq dict of float to ComplexNumber

    Mapping of frequency to complex voltage values.
    ia_freq dict of float to ComplexNumber

    Mapping of frequency to complex electrode current values.
    i_inj_freq dict of float to ComplexNumber

    Mapping of frequency to complex injection values. Defaults to an empty mapping for backwards compatibility.

    Examples:

    >>> import groundinsight as gi
>>> from groundinsight.api.examples import build_minimal
>>> bus = gi.run_fault(build_minimal(), "fault").buses[2]
>>> bus.name, round(bus.uepr, 2), round(abs(bus.uepr_freq[50.0]), 2)
('bus3', 18.03, 18.03)

    ResultReductionFactor ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Reduction-factor result at the fault bus.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    name (str, optional)

    The name of the reduction factor result.
    fault_bus str

    The bus where the fault occurred.
    value dict of float to float, optional

    Mapping from frequency to the EPR-based reduction factor r(f) = |u_fault with mutual| / |u_fault without mutual|. This is the quantity that reproduces the familiar closed form r = |1 - Z_mutual / Z_self| for a single shielded line. It is structurally independent of the impedance at the fault bus. None where the denominator is rounding noise -- below 1e-9 of the EPR the fault current alone would cause at the fault bus, |I_F| * |Z_FF| -- with a ModelAssumptionWarning REDUCTION_FACTOR_UNDEFINED (P9).
    value_current dict of float to float, optional

    Mapping from frequency to the current-based reduction factor r_I(f) = |I_E| / |I_F| -- the measured definition. I_E is the sum of the electrode currents of every bus that feeds the soil, not the electrode current at the faulted station: where the stations are bonded through continuous cable shields the current spreads along them and leaks into the soil at every one of them. Taking only the faulted station understates it by a factor of 1.8 to 4.7 on the verification feeder, depending on where the fault sits. Unlike value this factor responds to the fault-bus characteristic, which is what makes it usable as the ordinate of a rho-f sensitivity study. None per frequency where the frequency carries no fault current, and where no electrode carries more than 1e-9 of the fault current -- the current then returns through the shields and I_E is zero to within rounding; the latter comes with a ModelAssumptionWarning EARTH_GROUP_UNDEFINED (P9).
    i_earth dict of float to complex, optional

    The earth-return current I_E itself, per frequency, so a study can read the ampere value rather than only the ratio. Electrode currents at or below 1e-9 of the largest one are rounding noise and join neither group; None where value_current is None.
    earth_buses dict of float to list of str, optional

    The buses counted as feeding the soil at each frequency -- from the fault outwards, in every direction, up to where the potential profile turns. Reported because the split is a modelling statement and should be inspectable; see :mod:groundinsight.utils.earth_current.
    i_fault dict of float to complex, optional

    The fault current I_F = 3*I_0 the current-based factor divides by: sum(scaling * I_src) over the sources that reach the fault, a source on the fault bus included. For a Thevenin source this is its Norton current E / Z_src. None where no source has a value.
    u_earthing dict of float to complex, optional

    The earthing voltage U_E of EN 50522: the EPR at the fault bus, in the package's sign convention -- the same complex number as ResultBus.uepr_freq of the fault bus. This is the voltage the touch-voltage assessment starts from; in the norm's ideal case (a fault far from the infeed on a long bonded run) it equals r * |I_F| * |Z_E| with r = |1 - Z_m/Z_s| (value).
    z_earthing dict of float to complex, optional

    The earthing impedance Z_E of EN 50522: the driving-point impedance of the earthing network at the fault bus -- the voltage one ampere injected at the fault bus raises it to against remote earth, with every electrode and shield in place, without the inductive coupling and without the Thevenin loop closures of voltage sources (those belong to the fault loop, not to the earthing system). It is what an earthing-impedance measurement at the station would see, including the stations bonded to it through cable shields, and on a long homogeneous run it tends to the ladder limit -Z'/2 + sqrt(Z'^2/4 + Z_e*Z'). Equal to ResultGroundingImpedance.value. None only when the fault bus reaches remote earth through nothing but a Thevenin loop -- no bus connected to it through shields carries an electrode -- which is decided by that structure, not by the solver (EARTHING_IMPEDANCE_UNDEFINED).
    u_earthing_group dict of float to complex, optional

    Diagnostic: the current-weighted mean potential of the earth group earth_buses. On a long bonded run it lies 43 % below the fault-bus EPR, because the group reaches into the decaying tail of the potential profile.
    z_earthing_group dict of float to complex, optional

    Diagnostic: u_earthing_group / i_earth. The chain u_earthing_group = I_F * z_earthing_group * value_current closes on it by construction, which is why it is no check of anything.
    Notes

    Fault-bus quantities, not group means. u_earthing and z_earthing are taken at the fault bus. The group means come out 43 % / 45 % below the EPR and the driving-point impedance at the fault in the norm's ideal case -- unconservative if taken as U_E for a touch-voltage assessment -- and are kept as the *_group diagnostics only.

    Stored results in the group format. A record without i_fault, u_earthing_group and z_earthing_group holds the group means in u_earthing / z_earthing. It still loads: its values are moved to the *_group fields and u_earthing / z_earthing stay empty until the fault is solved again, so no stored number claims a meaning it was not computed with.

    ComplexNumber ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Pydantic-compatible complex number with real and imaginary parts.

    Wraps the native :class:complex type so that Pydantic models can serialise and deserialise complex numbers through JSON.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    real float

    The real part of the complex number.
    imag float

    The imaginary part of the complex number.
    Notes

    Non-finite parts are serialised as the strings "inf", "-inf" and "nan" rather than as the bare JavaScript-style Infinity / NaN literals Python's json module emits. inf is a load-bearing value here -- it is the open-end sentinel produced by the "nan" impedance formula -- so it must survive a round-trip, and the file must stay RFC 8259 JSON: SQLite's json_valid() returns 0 for Infinity, and a browser's JSON.parse refuses it outright, which would make every stored network with an open end unreadable to anything but Python. The validator already accepts those strings, so the round-trip is symmetric.

    Examples:

    >>> from groundinsight import ComplexNumber
>>> z = ComplexNumber(real=3.0, imag=4.0)
>>> abs(z), complex(z)
(5.0, (3+4j))
>>> z * 2
ComplexNumber(real=6.0, imag=8.0)
>>> ComplexNumber.model_validate("1+2j")
ComplexNumber(real=1.0, imag=2.0)

    __eq__ ¶

    __eq__(other)

    Compare against anything convertible; defer otherwise.

    Returning NotImplemented instead of raising is what the data model asks for: Python then tries the reflected operation and finally falls back to identity, so z == None is False rather than a TypeError. Every Optional[ComplexNumber] field in this package is compared against None somewhere, and the raising version turned that ordinary check into a crash.

    def __eq__(self, other):
    """Compare against anything convertible; defer otherwise.

    Returning ``NotImplemented`` instead of raising is what the data
    model asks for: Python then tries the reflected operation and finally
    falls back to identity, so ``z == None`` is ``False`` rather than a
    ``TypeError``. Every ``Optional[ComplexNumber]`` field in this package
    is compared against ``None`` somewhere, and the raising version turned
    that ordinary check into a crash.
    """
    try:
        other = self._convert_to_complex_number(other)
    except TypeError:
        return NotImplemented
    return self.real == other.real and self.imag == other.imag

    def __hash__(self):
    """Hash as the equivalent :class:`complex`.

    Defining ``__eq__`` sets ``__hash__`` to ``None``, which made
    ``ComplexNumber`` unusable as a dict key or set member. Hashing the
    equivalent ``complex`` keeps the hash/eq contract across the types
    this class compares equal to: ``hash(ComplexNumber(real=1, imag=0))``
    equals ``hash(1.0)``.
    """
    return hash(complex(self.real, self.imag))

    @field_validator("real", "imag", mode="before")
def convert_to_float(cls, value: Any) -> float:
    """Coerce ``real`` / ``imag`` inputs to ``float``; ``None`` becomes ``NaN``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    value : Any
        Numeric input to coerce. ``None`` is interpreted
        as ``numpy.nan``.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The coerced value.
    """
    if value is None:
        return np.nan
    return float(value)

    @model_validator(mode="before")
@classmethod
def validate_complex(cls, value: Any) -> Union["ComplexNumber", dict]:
    """
    Validates and converts the input value to a ComplexNumber instance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    value : Any
        The value to validate and convert. Can be a
        ``ComplexNumber``, ``complex``, ``float``, ``int``,
        ``dict`` or ``str``.

    Returns
    -------
    Union[ComplexNumber, dict]
        Either the original
    ``ComplexNumber`` instance (passed through) or a dictionary
    with ``real`` and ``imag`` keys ready for Pydantic to
    instantiate ``ComplexNumber``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the input string cannot be parsed as a complex number.
    TypeError
        If the input type is unsupported.
    """
    if isinstance(value, cls):
        return value
    elif isinstance(value, complex):
        return {"real": value.real, "imag": value.imag}
    elif isinstance(value, (float, int)):
        return {"real": float(value), "imag": 0.0}
    elif isinstance(value, dict):
        return value
    elif isinstance(value, str):
        try:
            c = complex(value.replace(" ", "").replace("i", "j"))
            return {"real": c.real, "imag": c.imag}
        except ValueError as error:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid complex number string: {value}") from error
    elif isinstance(value, (np.generic, numbers.Complex)):
        # NumPy scalars reach the models straight from the solver arrays;
        # ``np.complex128`` happens to subclass ``complex`` but
        # ``np.complex64`` and the integer types do not, and a bare
        # TypeError for them would name neither the value nor the model.
        try:
            c = complex(value)
        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise TypeError(
                f"Cannot parse ComplexNumber from type {type(value)}"
            ) from exc
        return {"real": c.real, "imag": c.imag}
    else:
        raise TypeError(f"Cannot parse ComplexNumber from type {type(value)}")
